subject: Dig (Peacock series)
query: is dig based on a book
title: Is Dig based on a book? Yes, Kate Myers' novel 'Excavations'
answer: Yes. Peacock's "Dig," the Amy Poehler and Hugh Laurie comedy premiering Nov. 23, 2026, is based on Kate Myers' 2023 comic novel "Excavations," about four women on a chaotic archaeological dig in Greece. It is fiction, not a true story, though Myers studied archaeology.
body:
"Dig" comes from "Excavations," a 288-page novel by Kate Myers published by HarperVia on July 4, 2023. The book follows four women on a summer excavation in Greece run by a domineering professor: Zara, who returns six years after a breakup on the same dig; Kara, who runs the site lab and is engaged to Zara's ex; Elise, a highly respected excavator without academic credentials; and Patty, an undergraduate intern who knows little about archaeology. Rivalries, romance and two missing ancient discuses push the dig toward disaster.

The Peacock series keeps the setup but reshapes it. Amy Poehler plays Elise, the lead archaeologist, who has long expected her boss to retire and hand her the dig. Hugh Laurie plays that boss, a British professor named Neville. Geraldine Viswanathan plays Dylan, Antonia Thomas plays Clare and Fina Strazza plays Patty, with Kayvan Novak, Jon Pointing and Bonita Friedericy in recurring roles. In the show, the team uncovers a rare find in southern Greece that pulls them into an international conspiracy.

The series was created by Poehler and Mike Schur, who worked together on "Parks and Recreation," with J.J. Philbin as co-showrunner. Myers is an executive producer. It was filmed in Los Angeles and on location in Greece. All 10 episodes arrive on Peacock at once on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026.

Is any of it real? No. The novel and the show are invented stories, and the excavation and its finds are fictional. The realism comes from the author: Myers studied archaeology at the University of Pennsylvania before writing for Elle, BuzzFeed and Self and working in TV development, and reviewers praised the book's convincing picture of daily life on a dig.
in_the_news: "Dig" premieres on Peacock on Nov. 23, 2026, with all 10 episodes at once.
